title: Book One · Chapter 43: The Long Way Home
story:
The boys look at their map. They find a short line behind the shops. It seems shorter than the school road.

The line runs behind the oil shop. It crosses a little square. Then it comes out near the painted bird. Leo traces it with a finger before the morning bell.

“We could get home before everyone else.”

“Or leave later,” Ronan says.

They laugh. But they cannot try a new route alone. They need an adult with them. After school, they ask Mum. Mum has no deliveries that afternoon. She can look at the path with them.

At the oil shop, the path is wide enough. A man is sweeping grit from his doorway. The man moves his broom out of the path. Then the boys walk past.

Farther in, the lane becomes narrow. A stack of empty baskets stands against one wall. The map doesn't have room for baskets. Ronan puts a small mark beside the line anyway.

Then they reach a metal gate.

It is closed, with a chain across the middle. A paper notice hangs above the handle. Leo reaches out, then pulls his hand back. He does not touch the chain.

“What does it say?” Ronan asks Mum.

“Private yard. No way through.”

“But the map goes through,” Leo says.

“We drew a line through here,” Ronan says. “But we didn't check the gate.”

He looks at the closed gate again. Now they need to walk all the way back. He sits for a moment to rest his feet.

A woman comes from a side door with a bucket. Mum speaks to her. The woman remembers the old store. “They kept this gate open then,” she says. “The store was busy.” Now the store is closed. People still come to that gate. They expect a way out.

“We're making a small map,” Ronan tells her.

“Then put the closed gate on it. I tell people about it three times a day. Your map can help them, too.”

She isn't angry, only busy. Mum thanks her, and they turn around.

Leo makes a heavy cross on the old route. Ronan adds the date. The gate may open again one day. Then they can change the mark. The date is their last check date.

At the oil shop, two older children pass them. The children walk toward the passage. “You cannot get through there,” Leo says. “I used it last year,” one child answers.

“It's chained today,” Ronan says.

The child looks past them, then decides to go the main road. He doesn't thank them. Ronan smiles at his new choice of road.

The boys hoped for a snack at home. Now they are late and hungry. Mum cuts one piece of bread into three. She takes the smallest piece for herself.

Ronan notices. He gives her a little of his.

“I had lunch,” she says.

“So did I.”

She takes the piece. She and Ronan eat beside each other.

The boys are fixing the map. Dad comes in. “Why did you cross out the shortcut?” he asks. Leo tells Dad about the notice. Then he tells Dad about the woman and her old store.

“Did you find another way?” Dad asks.

“The old way,” Ronan says.

Dad nods. “That road is still open. Good.”

The boys compare their walking times. Leo is ready to go home soon. This walk took longer than the school road. They walked back from the gate. They cannot call it a shortcut now. Ronan writes CHECKED, CLOSED beside the line and puts the pencil down.

The map is less pretty now, with crosses and dates. Now it clearly shows the locked gate. A visitor can choose the open road. He runs a finger along the ordinary school road, past the painted bird. They know every turn on that road. None of its gates is locked. They can still use it tomorrow.

---

重点表达：shortcut＝近路；notice＝告示；closed＝关着的；gate＝门。

辅助理解：chain＝链条；broom＝扫帚；cross out＝画线划掉。

理解问题：

1. 两人原以为的近路为什么走不通？
2. 这次 Ronan 怎样处理“不知道”的情况？
